findings.text: `int(nth)` silently wraps for wide or unsigned types. For example, a uint64 of 2^64-1 becomes -1, so Nth returns the last element instead of an out-of-bounds error. On 32-bit platforms an int64 such as 1<<32 truncates to 0 and returns the first element.

raw:
The `int(nth)` conversion can wrap for large values. A uint64 value such as 1<<63 becomes a negative int. If that wrapped value is at least -l, the function returns an element instead of an error. For example, uint64(2^64-1) becomes -1 and returns the last element. A uint8 is safe. An int64 is fine on 64-bit platforms but truncates on 32-bit ones.

The patch doesn't show whether the `constraints` import exists, and I can't check it, so I'm not reporting that.
